contradictions.topic: company_status_active: registry status is Amalgamated, not Active
contradictions.benign: The company was lawfully merged into a successor entity; certificates and dispatch notes in the old name are transition paperwork during the changeover.
contradictions.malicious: A defunct company's letterhead and identity are being used as a shell to certify counterfeit goods.
contradictions.resolution: The registry itself documents the succession mechanism (status 'Amalgamated'), which is exactly the benign explanation — but only the NCLT scheme order can confirm the invoicing entity is the lawful successor. Unresolvable from this dossier alone.

contradictions.topic: gstin_state_matches_claim: GSTIN registered in Gujarat, documents claim Tamil Nadu
contradictions.benign: Post-merger GST consolidation at the successor's Vadodara head office while production continues at the Coimbatore plant — the invoice says exactly this.
contradictions.malicious: A real GSTIN was lifted from an unrelated Gujarat firm to dress up forged Tamil Nadu paperwork.
contradictions.resolution: The benign mechanism is the same amalgamation the authoritative registry documents; the two anomalies share one explanation. The successor's GST registration certificate would settle it. Not resolvable from this dossier.

contradictions.topic: cross_doc_field_drift: company name differs between certificate and invoice
contradictions.benign: Certificate issued in the manufacturing entity's name, invoice in the successor's billing name — normal during an amalgamation transition.
contradictions.malicious: Documents forged separately with inconsistent identities.
contradictions.resolution: Heuristic-tier drift is subsumed by the amalgamation explanation above; it cannot outweigh authoritative-tier context. Follows the same unresolved conflict.

narrative: Every anomaly in this dossier — the non-Active status, the out-of-state GSTIN, the name drift between certificate and invoice — is consistent with one benign mechanism that the authoritative registry itself documents: the company was amalgamated into a successor. But the same pattern is also how a defunct identity gets misused. No finding is dispositive, and the tie sits at the authoritative tier, so it cannot be resolved by lower-tier evidence. One artefact decides it: the NCLT scheme-of-amalgamation order naming the successor entity.
